1.text: A Psalm of David. The LORD Himself is my shepherd, the One who feeds me, leads me, and guards me as His own, so I shall never lack for any good thing I truly need.
1.amp: A Psalm of David. The LORD Himself is my shepherd [ro'i -- the One who pastures His flock: feeding, leading, and guarding them]; so I shall never lack [chaser -- be without] any good thing I truly need.
1.notes: ra'ah (H7462) = to shepherd/tend/feed; chaser (H2637) = to lack. The whole psalm unfolds this single image of the LORD as shepherd and host.

2.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters that refresh me.
2.amp: He makes me lie down in green pastures [deshe -- where the flock rests, content and well-fed]; He leads me gently [nahal -- at the pace of the weak] beside quiet waters [menuchah -- still waters of refreshment, calm enough that a sheep can drink unafraid].
2.notes: deshe (H1877) = fresh pasture grass (rest and fullness); nahal (H5095) = to lead gently to a resting place; menuchah (H4496) = rest/quietness -- still waters that refresh.

3.text: He restores my soul, bringing my life back when it is drained and wandering; and He guides me along the well-worn paths of righteousness, for the honor of His own name is staked on leading me home.
3.amp: He restores my soul [shuv nephesh -- He turns my life back, reviving what was spent and strayed]; He guides me in the tracks of righteousness [ma'gal -- the well-worn ruts of the right way] for His name's sake [His own reputation is bound up in it].
3.notes: shuv (H7725) = to bring back/restore; ma'gal (H4570) = a track worn by use; led 'for His name's sake' = staked on God's honor.

4.text: Even when I walk through the valley of deepest darkness -- the very shadow of death, thick with dread -- I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod to drive off the wolves and Your staff to draw me back, they protect and comfort me.
4.amp: Even when I walk through the valley of deepest darkness [tsalmaveth -- the death-dark shadow, the ravine where the dread of dying presses in], I will fear no evil, for You are with me [the psalm turns here from 'He' to 'You,' God now walking at my side]; Your rod [shevet -- the club that beats off predators] and Your staff [the crook that pulls me back from the edge], they protect and comfort me.
4.notes: tsalmaveth (H6757) = shadow of death / deepest gloom. The pronoun shifts from 'He' to 'You' -- nearness in danger. shevet (H7626) = rod/club for defense (protects); mish'enet (H4938) = staff for support and rescue (comforts).

5.text: You prepare a table before me, a full feast spread out in the very presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil, welcoming me as an honored guest; and my cup of blessing overflows.
5.amp: You prepare a table before me [arak -- set out and arrange a banquet] in the presence of my enemies [while they look on, powerless to touch me]; You anoint my head with oil [dashen -- the customary welcome poured out for an honored guest]; my cup of blessing overflows [revayah -- filled past the brim, saturated].
5.notes: arak (H6186) = to arrange/set in order (a table/feast); dashen (H1878) = to anoint richly -- the host's welcome for an esteemed guest (cf. Luke 7:46); revayah (H7310) = overflow/saturation.

6.text: Surely goodness and covenant-love, God's loyal and unbreakable mercy, will pursue me, hunting me down all the days of my life; and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for the length of my days, and on without end.
6.amp: Surely goodness and covenant-love [chesed -- loyal, unbreakable mercy] will pursue me [radaph -- chase me down, the way enemies once did] all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for the length of my days [Heb. 'orek yamim -- and beyond].
6.notes: chesed (H2617) = covenant lovingkindness/loyal love; radaph (H7291) = to pursue/chase (often of a hunter) -- here goodness 'hunts me down'; 'forever' = 'orek yamim, 'length of days.'
